> bitcoinjs-lib
# bitcoinjs-lib: JavaScript Bitcoin library

> A JavaScript Bitcoin library for node.js and browsers.
> Written in TypeScript with committed JS output files.
> MIT License. 5,974 GitHub stars.

## Overview

bitcoinjs-lib is a pure JavaScript/TypeScript implementation of Bitcoin primitives for node.js and browsers. It provides low-level Bitcoin operations including transaction building, script construction, payment templates (P2PKH, P2SH, P2WPKH, P2WSH, P2TR), PSBT (BIP174/371), address encoding, and Merkle tree operations. It follows Bitcoin Core consensus and policy standards.

## Architecture

- Source is written in TypeScript (ts_src/)
- TypeScript is transpiled to JavaScript (src/) which is committed to the repo
- Dual package: ESM (tsconfig.json) + CJS (tsconfig.cjs.json)
- Tests use Mocha with tsx loader (test/*.spec.ts)
- Coverage thresholds: 85% branches, 90% functions, 90% lines

## Key Source Files

- ts_src/index.ts — Main entry point, exports all public API
- ts_src/transaction.ts — Transaction class (build, sign, verify)
- ts_src/script.ts — Bitcoin script assembly/decompilation
- ts_src/payments/ — Payment template implementations (p2pkh, p2sh, p2wpkh, p2wsh, p2tr, p2ms, p2pk, embed, lazy, bip341)
- ts_src/psbt.ts — PSBT v0/v2 (BIP174/BIP371) implementation
- ts_src/psbt/ — PSBT utilities and BIP371 Taproot extensions
- ts_src/address.ts — Address encoding/decoding (bech32, base58check)
- ts_src/crypto.ts — Hash functions (SHA256, SHA512, HMAC) via @noble/hashes
- ts_src/ecc_lib.ts — Elliptic curve interface (secp256k1)
- ts_src/networks.ts — Bitcoin network definitions (mainnet, testnet, etc.)
- ts_src/block.ts — Block Merkle root calculation
- ts_src/merkle.ts — Merkle tree utilities
- ts_src/bip66.ts — BIP66 DER signature encoding
- ts_src/bufferutils.ts — Buffer/Uint8Array utility functions
- ts_src/ops.ts — Opcode constants and buffer operations
- ts_src/push_data.ts — Script push data operations
- ts_src/script_number.ts — Script number encoding
- ts_src/script_signature.ts — Script signature parsing

## Key Dependencies

- @noble/hashes — SHA256, SHA512, HMAC (no native deps)
- bech32 — Bech32/Bech32m address encoding
- bip174 — PSBT BIP174 interfaces
- bs58check — Base58Check encoding
- uint8array-tools — Uint8Array/Buffer utilities
- valibot — Runtime type validation
- varuint-bitcoin — Variable-length integer encoding

## Build Commands

- npm run build — Clean, compile TS→JS (ESM + CJS), format JS output
- npm test — Build + format check + lint + coverage
- npm run lint — ESLint on ts_src/ and src/
- npm run format — Prettier on ts/ and test files
- npm run unit — Build + unit tests
- npm run integration — Build + integration tests (slow, 50s timeout)
- npm run doc — Generate TypeDoc documentation

## Code Style

- Prettier: single quotes, trailing comma all, arrow parens avoid, tab width 2, end of line auto
- ESLint: @typescript-eslint/recommended + prettier integration
- TypeScript strict mode
- All JS files are committed (transpiled output is verified)
- Commits must be atomic with readable diffs
- PRs should be focused: one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor

## Contribution Guidelines

- Fork and create a topic branch
- Run npm run build then npm test before submitting
- Both .ts source and compiled .js/.d.ts files must be committed together
- Verify JS output matches TS changes (git diff)
- Focused patchsets (one concern per PR)
- Maintainers may request squash/rebase before merge
- No CLA required
- GitHub is preferred communication; Matrix (#bitcoinjs-dev:matrix.org) and IRC (#bitcoinjs on libera.chat) available

## Bitcoin Policy Alignment

- Creation operations follow Bitcoin Core IsStandard policy
- Validation operations are consensus-bound only (non-standard data accepted)
- ECDSA signatures follow LOW_S standard by default

## Testing

- Unit tests: test/*.spec.ts (Mocha + tsx)
- Integration tests: test/integration/*.ts
- Coverage: c8 with thresholds (branches 85%, functions 90%, lines 90%)
- Fixtures: test/fixtures/

## Important Notes

- Only tagged releases are stable; master is the development branch
- The library is designed for auditability — verify, don't trust
- Browser and Node.js compatible (via Buffer polyfills)
- No native dependencies — pure JavaScript
